column1: # tests/coverage-floor.tsv - Q11: coverage may not go down.
# One row per file the host tier builds: the line-coverage percentage
# below which `make coverage-check` fails. Raised by hand, with the
# commit that raised it, exactly like tests/budgets.tsv - and lowered by
# hand too, because deleting a test can be the right call and should have
# to be said out loud rather than happening quietly.
# Q8 deliberately set no coverage *target*, and that still stands: the
# absolute number is whatever the tests honestly reach. This constrains
# A caveat worth carrying next to these numbers: line coverage is the
# weaker of the two instruments here. `net/ethernet.c` sat at 100% lines
# with a **0%** mutation score until Q12 looked - every line ran and
# nothing asserted what any of them did. Read this file next to
# M101: the names here are repo-relative paths, and they used to be
# relative to kernel/ instead. llvm-cov prints each file with the longest
# common prefix of everything on its command line removed, so adding the
# first user-space source to the report shortened nothing and lengthened
# every kernel name. Every floor in this file stopped matching, and the
# ratchet reported ten "new" files and "nothing fell" - which is a
# ratchet that has quietly stopped ratcheting. tools/coverage-ratchet.py
# now fails when a name in this file is absent from the report, so the
# next time that happens it is an error rather than a silence.
# M100: the floors are the MEASURED number now, not a round number under
# it, and every file in the report has one.
# Both changes are the same repair. Rounding 83.82 down to 83 meant the
# ratchet printed "raised ... raise it, and say so" for seven files on
# every run, forever, and eight more files had no row at all and printed
# "new" on every run. Fifteen lines of advice nobody was going to act on,
# on every single run - and underneath them, two floors that had actually
# FALLEN and had been falling since M98. The noise is what hid them.
# So: exact values, and tools/coverage-ratchet.py now fails on a file
# with no row rather than printing one more line. The report should be
# silent when nothing changed, because that is the only state in which

column4: Every line. Mutation score 73.8%, which is the more interesting number.
Mutation score 89.4% after Q12's split and coalescing tests.
The error paths are covered; the indirect and double-indirect block chains largely are not.
M100: exact rather than 83, for the reason in this file's header.
M100: exact rather than 62. The send path was entirely unexercised until Q12.
M100: exact rather than 74. Mutation score 59.4%; the unreachable part is the error-message paths.
M100: exact rather than 96. Was 28% before Q12's checksum tests. Mutation score 80.5%.
Was 90% lines at a 0% mutation score - the file that proved why this table is not enough on its own.

M100: exact rather than 62. Was 3.74% and the largest hole in the suite from Q8 until Q11. tests/test_tcp_states.c drives the eleven-state machine one segment at a time and found two remotely-triggerable defects on its first run.

M100: 89.55% until M100, and under this floor since M98 - three fw_cfg switches were added (bootstrap, pytest, pybuild) and the test that exists to catch a shared cache between them was grown for the first two and not the third. Its own comment had warned about exactly that, three lines above the table it needed a row in. 100% now: the switch table in tests/test_fwcfg.c is derived from one array, every switch is asked on every case, and each is asked twice.

M100: exact rather than 97. M101: the profile report's symbol resolver, and the first user-space file in this tier. The two uncovered lines are the guards for a symbol file that is not ascending, which the parser cannot produce and only a hand-written one can. Four hand-run mutations against its tests were all caught, which is the number that matters more than this one.

M100: the entropy source, ChaCha20 (RFC 7539) under a fast-key-erasure pool. The uncovered lines are the RDRAND/RDSEED path, which is #if'd out under LEANOS_HOST_TEST because the host test cannot hold a hardware generator still - graded on the machine by the [rng] marker instead, and by tests/test_random.c against the RFC vector for everything the host can reach.

M100: first floor. POSIX record locks, the table sqlite's transactions take three of. The one uncovered line is claim()'s NULL return, which flock_set makes unreachable by counting free entries first - and the mutation harness agrees, its one survivor there being that return. Mutation score 91.5%; the other nine survivors are `<` to `<=` on the table's loop bounds, a one-past-the-end read that only a sanitizer sees and the campaign runs without one.
M100: first floor. M85's pseudo-terminals, every line reached by tests/test_pty.c.
M100: first floor. The line discipline - canonical and raw modes, signals, job control. The uncovered part is the paths that need a real framebuffer console under them.

M120: 51.00 -> 50.83, and LOWERED deliberately rather than quietly - this file's header asks for that to be said out loud. M120 added two branches to sched.c that this tier structurally cannot reach: the memfd case in fill_one_page_ex and in sched_release_shared_range, both of which need a real address space with real page tables under them. They are graded on the machine instead, by [m120], and sharply: the child in /bin/memfdtest reads bytes the parent wrote, which only works if the fault path maps the object's own frame. The three region-reference helpers M120 also added ARE covered here (tests/test_memfd.c), because they are the dangerous half - one reference too few frees memory two processes are reading. M119: 50.40 -> 51.00 - fd_release and fd_retain grew three more cases (FD_EVENT, FD_TIMER, FD_EPOLL) and tests/test_readyfds.c drives all three, which matters more than the number: the union means every kind is the same bits, so a case that unref'd the wrong KIND would compile, run, and leak. M118: 49.86 -> 50.40, and the raise is claimed here because it is this milestone's: fd_release and fd_retain grew an FD_UNIX case each and tests/test_unixsock.c drives both. M100: first floor, and the most overdue row in this file. 2,157 lines, in the host tier since Q13 against a fake timer and a fake CPU, and until M100 nothing constrained its direction at all - it printed "new" on every run for as long as nobody read past the summary. Half the file is the multi-core and signal-delivery paths that Q13's harness does not drive yet; raising this is the measurable half of the queue's row 5.
M100: first floor. One line, and M99 is the milestone that proved it matters - five syscalls returned -1 over an untouched errno and the visible symptom was print() writing nothing and exiting 0.
M100: first floor. The uncovered part is the character-class names inside bracket expressions.
M100: first floor.
M100: first floor. dirname and basename, both entirely reached.

M117: 48.50 -> 48.24. Not a test removed: `make coverage` had not compiled since M111 (its CFLAGS lacked -Iuser_space/library and -DLEANOS_HOST_TEST, which every other host build has), and with them wchar.c compiles three lines the tests never reached. M100: first floor, and the honest number for a file that exists because GNU hello's first line asked for it (M94). Half of it is the wide stdio family, which nothing in the host tier calls.
M117: first floor, set where M116's test left it - the ring model against every frame length.
M117: first floor, set where the M114 resolver tests left it.
M117: first floor, set where M112's tree-walk tests left it.
M117: first floor, set where M111's package tests left it.
M117: first floor - the differential test against the host reaches every line.
M117: first floor - M116's four tests at every phase reach every line.

M119: first floor. A counter you can wait on. The three uncovered lines are the heap-failure path in eventfd_create. Mutation score 87.5% - 50% on the first run, and the nine tests that closed the gap were mostly null guards and a reference count nothing had taken twice.

M119: first floor. The four uncovered lines are the heap-failure path. Mutation score 83.3%. Every function takes the time as an argument, which is why a test can ask what this file does at 1099.999 ms - see its header for why that decision was made against tcp.c's precedent rather than in ignorance of it.

M120: first floor. Shared memory a descriptor names. The three uncovered lines are the heap-failure path in memfd_truncate's array growth. Mutation score 89.3% - 82.1% on the first run, and two of the five survivors were assignments in memfd_init that nothing could notice, which is how that function came to do one thing instead of six.

M119: first floor, and the highest of the three because the readiness question is a function pointer: the set management is graded against a scripted readiness table with no descriptors under it at all. Mutation score 95.7%.

M119: 92.52 -> 93.11. The three accessors epoll needs (writable, hup, rdhup) arrived in M119 and are graded here rather than only through the kernel's epoll mask - which is the direction that matters, because nothing else would notice one of them answering backwards. M118: first floor. AF_UNIX and SCM_RIGHTS. The uncovered lines are the paths that need a heap failure (kmalloc returning NULL in unix_new) and the ring's two-chunk wraparound on a message that straddles the end of the buffer, which needs a 4 KiB-scale fixture rather than the short strings these tests use. Mutation score 87.2%; of the five survivors, three are equivalent mutations and two are one-past-the-end reads that only a sanitizer sees - and the campaign runs without one.

M127: first floor. M107 added this file to the host tier and no row here, which nothing said - the --full tier's coverage stage had not COMPILED since M125 (COV_CFLAGS was missing -Ithird_party/lvgl, and test_lvgl_keys.c includes lvgl.h), and coverage is a --full-only stage. The boot-report decoder is pure: bytes in, key events out, so 100% is what it should be.
M127: first floor, same M107 gap. The cycle bit is the whole point of the file and every branch of it is reachable from a test, because the ring is a data structure and not a device.

M127: first floor, same M107 gap. This is the one path QEMU cannot reach at all - its namespace has 512-byte blocks, so a 4Kn drive's read-modify-write split is dead code on this machine and would first execute on somebody's real filesystem. 100% here is not a nicety.

M127: first floor, same M107 gap - and the lowest of the four because the uncovered lines are the enumeration paths that need a fake device tree wider than the one tests/fakes/fake_pci.c builds. Raising this means more fixture, not more assertions about the same fixture.

M140: first floor, and it is a first floor rather than an earned raise. M130 last touched this file and no row was ever added, so the host tier has been building it with nothing constraining its direction. 40.18 is what the tests honestly reach today; Q8's rule stands that the absolute number is not a target.

M140: first floor, same story - M129 added the vector icon rasteriser and the ratchet has never named it. Read it next to `make mutate` rather than instead of it: tools/gen-icons.c does the sharp grading of this code, on the generated faces, and that is where a regression would show first.
